test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2024: Official Paper (Held On: 02 Jul, 2024 Shift 4)
subject: general
question: In which judgement did the Supreme Court extend the scope of Article 21 and observed that ‘the Right to education flows directly from the Right to life’?

options.text: Kharak Singh v State of UP
Malak Singh v State of Punjab
Neerja Choudhari v State of M. P
Mohini Jain v State of Karnataka

solution:
The correct answer is __**Mohini Jain v State of Karnataka**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Supreme Court of India, in the case of **Mohini Jain v State of Karnataka**, extended the scope of Article 21 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The judgement observed that the **Right to education flows directly from the Right to life**, which is guaranteed under Article 21.
 
• This landmark decision emphasized that the state is obligated to provide educational facilities to its citizens as a part of their fundamental rights.
 
• The ruling paved the way for subsequent decisions and legislations that strengthened the right to education in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 21** of the Indian Constitution states that "No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law."
 
• The interpretation of Article 21 has been broadened over the years to include various rights that are essential to the life and dignity of an individual.
 
• The **Right to Education Act**, 2009, which provides free and compulsory education to all children aged 6 to 14 years, was a significant step towards realizing the right recognized in the Mohini Jain case.
 
• The Constitution (Eighty-sixth Amendment) Act, 2002, also inserted Article 21A, explicitly making education a fundamental right for children in the specified age group.
